bias: Today is dominated by a single fresh catalyst -- the Iran-US ceasefire holding over the weekend -- which knocked oil down 7.4% and pulled US10Y/US30Y down roughly 1% and 0.7%, extending the disinflation-relief theme that started emerging Jul24-26. That's a genuine positive versus 'liquidity tightening' framing. But it's not a clean risk-on day: VIX reversed higher (+3.18%) after three straight sessions of easing, and the Jul26 semis/Korea selloff (SOXX, DRAM, EWY) continues today, just at a slower pace. Underneath, the plumbing backdrop hasn't moved at all -- TGA, reserves and WALCL are still sitting on the Jul22 H.4.1 vintage with the next print due Jul 30 -- so 'structural_liquidity: Neutral' reflects genuinely stale data, not an easing signal. With SK Hynix earnings and a guidance-light FOMC both landing in the next 24-48 hours, today's relief rally is worth respecting but not yet a full regime call.

counterargs.thesis: Disinflation relief rally extends, but vol and the semis/Korea complex haven't fully stabilized
supporting: Oil -7.37% to $82.73 on the Iran-US ceasefire holding; Brent below $90
US10Y/US30Y fell -1.00%/-0.74% today, extending the Jul24-26 curve easing
SOXX/DRAM/EWY declines decelerated sharply vs Jul26's shock-day moves
KOSPI +0.97% on reopening after the weekend closure
ALLY (+1.42%) and COF (+1.72%) both bounced, not confirming CACC's weakness
against: VIX reversed higher, +3.18% to 19.16, ending three sessions of easing
HY OAS is still sitting at Jul26's widened 2.77% -- the first real crack this cycle hasn't reverted
CACC extended its losing streak, -2.44% today on top of Jul26's -3.12%
DFII5/DFII10 real yields remain at Jul26's firmed levels (2.17%/2.43%) -- the TIPS market hasn't confirmed genuine easing
EWY's gap below its 20-day SMA widened further, to roughly -10.1% from -8.7%
SK Hynix earnings and a guidance-light FOMC both land within 48 hours -- confidence is capped at 39% for a reason
counterargs.read: The oil-driven yield rally is real and worth respecting -- it directly reverses the inflation-reacceleration risk that had been building since Jul 8 -- but it's landing on a backdrop that hadn't actually stabilized yet. VIX's reversal higher and CACC's continued slide say the Jul26 'idiosyncratic semis/Korea/credit crack' story isn't over, just decelerating. Structural liquidity is neither improving nor worsening today; it's simply stale, waiting on Jul 30's H.4.1 print. With SK Hynix earnings tomorrow and the FOMC the day after -- both binary, both un-hedged by forward guidance (no SEP) -- this reads as a relief bounce to trade tactically (duration, fading oil-linked inflation exposure) rather than a signal to fully re-risk into semis or Korea.
